sourceInformation.source: The Incredible Wizard (Astrocade,1982), a licensed adaptation of Bally/Midway’s Wizard of Wor. Original game by Tom McHugh, Scot Norris and Julie Malan; this game is an original inspired work.
sourceInformation.perspective: Fixed topdown arena, cardinal movement and aiming
sourceInformation.tech: JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Web Audio; full readable my-3D2dge0.89.1, commit8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691; official unmodified AI Hub session client1.4.0, commit35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869. No runtime asset downloads.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Native shaded volumetric pixel art, textured plum-stone dungeons, brass lanterns and cyan/violet occult light. Original code-native wardens, lantern rifles, three hunter anatomies, Gildwing, Wizard, resonators and portals; engine generic lantern primitives.
sourceInformation.animation: Native Humanoid and Blob rigs, original rifle attachment, procedural family anatomy, continuous gait/flap/cast/recoil/protection/celebration phases, native depth-sorted queues and presentation-only remote interpolation.
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-written title, dungeon, chase, Wizard, victory and defeat compositions using native synth; coded effects and finite formant-filtered Animalese-like gibberish. Music defaults to10%; separate master/music/effects/voice buses. No audio files. No human listening check.
sourceInformation.online: Standalone solo and simultaneous1–2-player couch co-op; real AI Hub1–2-player shared-world online co-op. Host-authoritative simulation,9Hz snapshots and12Hz input heartbeats, reliable transport, no-player server support. Online sessions are launched by Hub; no standalone matchmaking.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless state/rule tests, actual command-only seeded complete campaigns, native renderer checks, packaged file:// Chromium and WebKit touch/UI tests, Firefox smoke, virtual standard-mapped controllers, offline Web Audio sample tests, official Hub standard/host-leave/server harness at150±50ms latency and5%loss plus two-peer shared combat. Perfect Normal bot finished in257.717s; human first-run10–15minute target remains unverified. No physical controller/touch/iOS/TV or human playtest.
sourceInformation.research: Manual transcription https://ballyalley.com/cart_manuals/text_manuals/incredible_wizard.txt ; manual scan https://ballyalley.com/cart_manuals/pdf_manuals/Incredible_Wizard%2C_The.pdf ; December1982 feature https://vgpavilion.com/mags/1982/12/vi/conquering-the-incredible-wizard/ ; archived hardware frame at40s https://archive.org/details/IncredibleWizardBallyArcadeAstrocade1982 . Appearance observed; historical audio/AI details unknown.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux, Ubuntu26.04.1 on WSL2. Node24.21.0; Python Playwright1.63.0 with installed browser engines. Physical devices and human listening unavailable.

testingFeedback: 15 distinct implementation issues were found and fixed; assertions are not counted as bugs. Details are in evidence/issues.json.

3 were classified as critical/game-breaking: Continue restored state without room-entry checkpoint; load full save envelope for correct retry. Corrupt persisted simulation could reach renderer; validate version/room/entity arrays/tuning at storage boundary. Actor AI route refreshed per frame could overshoot a junction and familiar escape path loop; choose direction at each grid junction.

The seeded command-only complete campaign was most helpful: it checked all six chambers, finite replacement obligations, one-bolt ownership, hidden hunters, bells, portals, familiar bonuses and all three finale manifestations without cheats. The official no-player-host harness independently proved lifecycle readiness.

The initial renderer smoke fixture used numeric IDs and therefore missed a string-ID animation bug. It was replaced and supplemented with actual simulation state. Screenshot checks were reserved for composition and silhouettes.
engineFeedback: The readable native shape/material system, shaded procedural rigs, fixed-step headless advance and controller-aware Shell made a complete original game practical without external assets.

I initially assumed one-based seat IDs and numeric actor IDs in presentation. Actual zero-based seats/string IDs exposed those mistakes. Native pose names and full-engine asset signatures were checked against the handoff.

The authoritative serializable simulation: cardinal junction movement, swept one-bolt collisions, union-of-player cloak visibility, finite encounters, checkpoint fidelity and Hub host/client replication.
Keeping native projected drawing, cell-centered authoritative coordinates, independent device ownership and live online menus consistent across renderer, simulation and headless tests.

The vendored engine file is unchanged. Game extensions add original native assets/weapon and animations, invisible multitouch controls, explicit menu/gameplay input ownership, remote interpolation, and a Hub fixed-step pump with native live overlays/autoPause disabled online.
Add an official simultaneous network-ready arcade example with explicit input ownership, serializable state and invisible two-thumb touch controls.
promptFeedback: The distinctive source anchors and concrete mechanics/verification contracts made the game’s identity and acceptance criteria clear.
PLAN.md referred to naming rules in an own brief; TASK.md supplied the actual artifact names. Exact historical AI/audio and a human first-run duration could not be confirmed headlessly.
Finishing the same real six-room simulation across solo, couch co-op, online authority, attract play and command-only end-to-end tests while preserving hidden information.
Provide a small machine-readable handoff contract for the engine and Hub plus a single canonical deliverable schema; retain the freedom to author original assets and encounters.

aiHub.name: The Inconspicuous Wizard
aiHub.tagline: Six chambers. One shot at a time.
aiHub.description: Enter a pompous sorcerer’s menagerie with a lantern rifle that holds only one bolt. Read the radar, ring brass bells and cover a partner through six original chambers and a three-part Wizard finale.
aiHub.controls: WASD/left stick move; mouse/arrows/right stick aim; click/Space/R2/Cross fire; Escape/Options pause; invisible touch sticks with optional lane auto-fire.
